ZERO_THREE_LEFT.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
ZERO_THREE_LEFT.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
ZERO_THREE_LEFT.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

1529 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 22; a mismatch means the band carries little.

td.why: one row per band centre below; each row's own answer is the one to read, and the answer here only says whether ANY band centre reached one
td.power_feature: band power in the device's own least-significant-bit units, reached from the 250 samples-per-second voltage trace by the validated transform, or from the device's own spectrum where no voltage trace was in range
td.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. Each snapshot covers 30 s, so a row of N seconds takes the nearest ceil(N / 30) snapshots within the window, and a report without that many contributes nothing to that row -- which is why the taller rows can hold fewer reports than the short ones.

td.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
td.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
td.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

1494 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 22; a mismatch means the band carries little.

psd.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. Each snapshot covers 30 s, so a row of N seconds takes the nearest ceil(N / 30) snapshots within the window, and a report without that many contributes nothing to that row -- which is why the taller rows can hold fewer reports than the short ones.

psd.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
psd.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
psd.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

35 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 22; a mismatch means the band carries little.

counting.rule: a report with both TD and PSD in its window is counted in the TD-only grid (from its TD) and in the PSD-only grid (from its PSD), and once in the mixed grid (from its TD); so in every cell the mixed count is the TD count plus the PSD count over the reports with no TD

chronic_band_choice.method: each pain report takes the one chronic (10-minute) band-power reading whose 10 minutes cover the time it was filed (a reading's time is the start of its 10 minutes), on this contact pair and frequency, the device's value at face value; a report in a gap of the log has none and is counted; Pearson r against the pain score; interval: whole reports resampled in blocks (the heat map's method); p: every other rotation of the pain series once; the current-removed check is a warning only

ONE_THREE_LEFT.why: one row per band centre below; each row's own answer is the one to read, and the answer here only says whether ANY band centre reached one
ONE_THREE_LEFT.power_feature: band power in the device's own least-significant-bit units, reached from the 250 samples-per-second voltage trace by the validated transform, or from the device's own spectrum where no voltage trace was in range
ONE_THREE_LEFT.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. Each snapshot covers 30 s, so a row of N seconds takes the nearest ceil(N / 30) snapshots within the window, and a report without that many contributes nothing to that row -- which is why the taller rows can hold fewer reports than the short ones.

correlation_by_recording_source.is: the same Pearson correlation as the cell, on the same band-power values after the same outlier rule and the same matching, computed on the reports whose band power came from TD (the time-domain recording in 3 s pieces, used whenever any falls in the match window) alone, and on those whose band power came from PSD (the device's 30 s snapshots, used only when no TD does) alone; each with the cell's own interval method. Descriptive: it selects no band, sets no interval, q or verdict, and draws nothing.

best_correlation_rows.direction: band power falls as pain rises
best_correlation_rows.power_feature: band power in the device's own least-significant-bit units, reached from the 250 samples-per-second voltage trace by the validated transform, or from the device's own spectrum where no voltage trace was in range

ONE_THREE_LEFT.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
ONE_THREE_LEFT.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
ONE_THREE_LEFT.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

4841 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 18; a mismatch means the band carries little.

td.why: one row per band centre below; each row's own answer is the one to read, and the answer here only says whether ANY band centre reached one
td.power_feature: band power in the device's own least-significant-bit units, reached from the 250 samples-per-second voltage trace by the validated transform, or from the device's own spectrum where no voltage trace was in range
td.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. Each snapshot covers 30 s, so a row of N seconds takes the nearest ceil(N / 30) snapshots within the window, and a report without that many contributes nothing to that row -- which is why the taller rows can hold fewer reports than the short ones.

psd.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
psd.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
psd.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

45 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 21; a mismatch means the band carries little.

counting.rule: a report with both TD and PSD in its window is counted in the TD-only grid (from its TD) and in the PSD-only grid (from its PSD), and once in the mixed grid (from its TD); so in every cell the mixed count is the TD count plus the PSD count over the reports with no TD

chronic_band_choice.method: each pain report takes the one chronic (10-minute) band-power reading whose 10 minutes cover the time it was filed (a reading's time is the start of its 10 minutes), on this contact pair and frequency, the device's value at face value; a report in a gap of the log has none and is counted; Pearson r against the pain score; interval: whole reports resampled in blocks (the heat map's method); p: every other rotation of the pain series once; the current-removed check is a warning only

ZERO_TWO_LEFT.why: one row per band centre below; each row's own answer is the one to read, and the answer here only says whether ANY band centre reached one
ZERO_TWO_LEFT.power_feature: band power in the device's own least-significant-bit units, reached from the 250 samples-per-second voltage trace by the validated transform, or from the device's own spectrum where no voltage trace was in range
ZERO_TWO_LEFT.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. Each snapshot covers 30 s, so a row of N seconds takes the nearest ceil(N / 30) snapshots within the window, and a report without that many contributes nothing to that row -- which is why the taller rows can hold fewer reports than the short ones.

correlation_by_recording_source.is: the same Pearson correlation as the cell, on the same band-power values after the same outlier rule and the same matching, computed on the reports whose band power came from TD (the time-domain recording in 3 s pieces, used whenever any falls in the match window) alone, and on those whose band power came from PSD (the device's 30 s snapshots, used only when no TD does) alone; each with the cell's own interval method. Descriptive: it selects no band, sets no interval, q or verdict, and draws nothing.

ZERO_TWO_LEFT.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
ZERO_TWO_LEFT.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
ZERO_TWO_LEFT.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

1429 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 22; a mismatch means the band carries little.

td.why: one row per band centre below; each row's own answer is the one to read, and the answer here only says whether ANY band centre reached one
td.power_feature: band power in the device's own least-significant-bit units, reached from the 250 samples-per-second voltage trace by the validated transform, or from the device's own spectrum where no voltage trace was in range
td.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. Each snapshot covers 30 s, so a row of N seconds takes the nearest ceil(N / 30) snapshots within the window, and a report without that many contributes nothing to that row -- which is why the taller rows can hold fewer reports than the short ones.

td.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
td.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
td.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

1427 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 22; a mismatch means the band carries little.

psd.power_feature: band power in the device's own least-significant-bit units, reached from the 250 samples-per-second voltage trace by the validated transform, or from the device's own spectrum where no voltage trace was in range
psd.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. Each snapshot covers 30 s, so a row of N seconds takes the nearest ceil(N / 30) snapshots within the window, and a report without that many contributes nothing to that row -- which is why the taller rows can hold fewer reports than the short ones.

psd.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
psd.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
psd.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

2 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 21; a mismatch means the band carries little.

counting.rule: a report with both TD and PSD in its window is counted in the TD-only grid (from its TD) and in the PSD-only grid (from its PSD), and once in the mixed grid (from its TD); so in every cell the mixed count is the TD count plus the PSD count over the reports with no TD

chronic_band_choice.method: each pain report takes the one chronic (10-minute) band-power reading whose 10 minutes cover the time it was filed (a reading's time is the start of its 10 minutes), on this contact pair and frequency, the device's value at face value; a report in a gap of the log has none and is counted; Pearson r against the pain score; interval: whole reports resampled in blocks (the heat map's method); p: every other rotation of the pain series once; the current-removed check is a warning only

ZERO_THREE_RIGHT.why: one row per band centre below; each row's own answer is the one to read, and the answer here only says whether ANY band centre reached one
ZERO_THREE_RIGHT.power_feature: band power in the device's own least-significant-bit units, reached from the 250 samples-per-second voltage trace by the validated transform, or from the device's own spectrum where no voltage trace was in range
ZERO_THREE_RIGHT.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. Each snapshot covers 30 s, so a row of N seconds takes the nearest ceil(N / 30) snapshots within the window, and a report without that many contributes nothing to that row -- which is why the taller rows can hold fewer reports than the short ones.

correlation_by_recording_source.is: the same Pearson correlation as the cell, on the same band-power values after the same outlier rule and the same matching, computed on the reports whose band power came from TD (the time-domain recording in 3 s pieces, used whenever any falls in the match window) alone, and on those whose band power came from PSD (the device's 30 s snapshots, used only when no TD does) alone; each with the cell's own interval method. Descriptive: it selects no band, sets no interval, q or verdict, and draws nothing.

ZERO_THREE_RIGHT.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
ZERO_THREE_RIGHT.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
ZERO_THREE_RIGHT.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

6026 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 15; a mismatch means the band carries little.

td.why: one row per band centre below; each row's own answer is the one to read, and the answer here only says whether ANY band centre reached one
td.power_feature: band power in the device's own least-significant-bit units, reached from the 250 samples-per-second voltage trace by the validated transform, or from the device's own spectrum where no voltage trace was in range
td.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. Each snapshot covers 30 s, so a row of N seconds takes the nearest ceil(N / 30) snapshots within the window, and a report without that many contributes nothing to that row -- which is why the taller rows can hold fewer reports than the short ones.

td.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
td.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
td.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

5382 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 22; a mismatch means the band carries little.

psd.why: one row per band centre below; each row's own answer is the one to read, and the answer here only says whether ANY band centre reached one
psd.power_feature: band power in the device's own least-significant-bit units, reached from the 250 samples-per-second voltage trace by the validated transform, or from the device's own spectrum where no voltage trace was in range
psd.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. Each snapshot covers 30 s, so a row of N seconds takes the nearest ceil(N / 30) snapshots within the window, and a report without that many contributes nothing to that row -- which is why the taller rows can hold fewer reports than the short ones.

psd.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
psd.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
psd.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

644 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 21; a mismatch means the band carries little.

counting.rule: a report with both TD and PSD in its window is counted in the TD-only grid (from its TD) and in the PSD-only grid (from its PSD), and once in the mixed grid (from its TD); so in every cell the mixed count is the TD count plus the PSD count over the reports with no TD

chronic_band_choice.method: each pain report takes the one chronic (10-minute) band-power reading whose 10 minutes cover the time it was filed (a reading's time is the start of its 10 minutes), on this contact pair and frequency, the device's value at face value; a report in a gap of the log has none and is counted; Pearson r against the pain score; interval: whole reports resampled in blocks (the heat map's method); p: every other rotation of the pain series once; the current-removed check is a warning only

ONE_THREE_RIGHT.why: one row per band centre below; each row's own answer is the one to read, and the answer here only says whether ANY band centre reached one
ONE_THREE_RIGHT.power_feature: band power in the device's own least-significant-bit units, reached from the 250 samples-per-second voltage trace by the validated transform, or from the device's own spectrum where no voltage trace was in range
ONE_THREE_RIGHT.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. Each snapshot covers 30 s, so a row of N seconds takes the nearest ceil(N / 30) snapshots within the window, and a report without that many contributes nothing to that row -- which is why the taller rows can hold fewer reports than the short ones.

correlation_by_recording_source.is: the same Pearson correlation as the cell, on the same band-power values after the same outlier rule and the same matching, computed on the reports whose band power came from TD (the time-domain recording in 3 s pieces, used whenever any falls in the match window) alone, and on those whose band power came from PSD (the device's 30 s snapshots, used only when no TD does) alone; each with the cell's own interval method. Descriptive: it selects no band, sets no interval, q or verdict, and draws nothing.

ONE_THREE_RIGHT.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
ONE_THREE_RIGHT.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
ONE_THREE_RIGHT.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

1499 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 22; a mismatch means the band carries little.

td.why: one row per band centre below; each row's own answer is the one to read, and the answer here only says whether ANY band centre reached one
td.power_feature: band power in the device's own least-significant-bit units, reached from the 250 samples-per-second voltage trace by the validated transform, or from the device's own spectrum where no voltage trace was in range
td.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. Each snapshot covers 30 s, so a row of N seconds takes the nearest ceil(N / 30) snapshots within the window, and a report without that many contributes nothing to that row -- which is why the taller rows can hold fewer reports than the short ones.

td.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
td.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
td.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

1498 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 22; a mismatch means the band carries little.

psd.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. psd.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
psd.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
psd.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

1 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 11; a mismatch means the band carries little.

counting.rule: a report with both TD and PSD in its window is counted in the TD-only grid (from its TD) and in the PSD-only grid (from its PSD), and once in the mixed grid (from its TD); so in every cell the mixed count is the TD count plus the PSD count over the reports with no TD

chronic_band_choice.method: each pain report takes the one chronic (10-minute) band-power reading whose 10 minutes cover the time it was filed (a reading's time is the start of its 10 minutes), on this contact pair and frequency, the device's value at face value; a report in a gap of the log has none and is counted; Pearson r against the pain score; interval: whole reports resampled in blocks (the heat map's method); p: every other rotation of the pain series once; the current-removed check is a warning only

ZERO_TWO_RIGHT.why: one row per band centre below; each row's own answer is the one to read, and the answer here only says whether ANY band centre reached one
ZERO_TWO_RIGHT.power_feature: band power in the device's own least-significant-bit units, reached from the 250 samples-per-second voltage trace by the validated transform, or from the device's own spectrum where no voltage trace was in range
ZERO_TWO_RIGHT.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. Each snapshot covers 30 s, so a row of N seconds takes the nearest ceil(N / 30) snapshots within the window, and a report without that many contributes nothing to that row -- which is why the taller rows can hold fewer reports than the short ones.

correlation_by_recording_source.is: the same Pearson correlation as the cell, on the same band-power values after the same outlier rule and the same matching, computed on the reports whose band power came from TD (the time-domain recording in 3 s pieces, used whenever any falls in the match window) alone, and on those whose band power came from PSD (the device's 30 s snapshots, used only when no TD does) alone; each with the cell's own interval method. Descriptive: it selects no band, sets no interval, q or verdict, and draws nothing.

ZERO_TWO_RIGHT.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
ZERO_TWO_RIGHT.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
ZERO_TWO_RIGHT.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

1989 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 22; a mismatch means the band carries little.

td.power_feature: band power in the device's own least-significant-bit units, reached from the 250 samples-per-second voltage trace by the validated transform, or from the device's own spectrum where no voltage trace was in range
td.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. Each snapshot covers 30 s, so a row of N seconds takes the nearest ceil(N / 30) snapshots within the window, and a report without that many contributes nothing to that row -- which is why the taller rows can hold fewer reports than the short ones.

td.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
td.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
td.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

1989 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 22; a mismatch means the band carries little.

psd.why: one row per band centre below; each row's own answer is the one to read, and the answer here only says whether ANY band centre reached one
psd.power_feature: band power in the device's own least-significant-bit units, reached from the 250 samples-per-second voltage trace by the validated transform, or from the device's own spectrum where no voltage trace was in range
psd.device_spectrum_axis_note: A pain report with no voltage trace within the match window is answered from the device's own FFT snapshots instead. Each snapshot covers 30 s, so a row of N seconds takes the nearest ceil(N / 30) snapshots within the window, and a report without that many contributes nothing to that row -- which is why the taller rows can hold fewer reports than the short ones.

psd.auc_grid_is: the area under the curve of the band power itself, keeping its direction: above 0.5 the band power is higher on high-pain reports, below 0.5 it is lower, and 0.5 means neither
psd.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat
psd.pain_split_rule: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison
notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

0 single 3 s pieces more than 7 median absolute deviations above this contact's own median (per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: the pain scores slid along in time, all 807 ways (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 21; a mismatch means the band carries little.

counting.rule: a report with both TD and PSD in its window is counted in the TD-only grid (from its TD) and in the PSD-only grid (from its PSD), and once in the mixed grid (from its TD); so in every cell the mixed count is the TD count plus the PSD count over the reports with no TD

chronic_band_choice.method: each pain report takes the one chronic (10-minute) band-power reading whose 10 minutes cover the time it was filed (a reading's time is the start of its 10 minutes), on this contact pair and frequency, the device's value at face value; a report in a gap of the log has none and is counted; Pearson r against the pain score; interval: whole reports resampled in blocks (the heat map's method); p: every other rotation of the pain series once; the current-removed check is a warning only

device_timing_ranges.averaging_source: Medtronic BrainSense Tip Cards (2020, FIELDPORTAL1594651482409), p. 8
device_timing_ranges.averaging_caveat: The 0-30 s range is printed in the 2020 BrainSense tip card and was confirmed on the clinician tablet's Adaptive Therapy setup screen on 2026-09-15 (0.00 ms to 30.00 s, non-overlapping averages). This participant's device has run averaging from 100 ms to 30 s and never longer.
device_timing_ranges.onset_source: Clinician tablet (A610), Adaptive Therapy setup screens, read by the PI on 2026-09-15
device_timing_ranges.onset_note: The FDA summary (P960009/S478, Table 2) prints a Dual Threshold onset range of 0 to 6 min; the clinician tablet offers 0.00 ms to 30.00 s on both timers, and neither the white paper nor the A610 manual prints a range. The platform applies the tablet's 30 s, which is what can be typed.
device_timing_ranges.onset_meaning: The onset duration does not average: it holds an averaged reading past a threshold for this long before the device acts (Dual Threshold, 0 to 30 s on the tablet). A length of signal longer than the averaging range can only be approximated as a sustained level, not as a mean, and only up to one averaging window plus one onset hold.

stability_background.reason: the answer for this key is already stored

Left.why: stimulating on contact(s) 1, 2, the device senses only on the two contacts flanking them

Right.why: stimulating on contact(s) 1, 2, the device senses only on the two contacts flanking them

sensing_rule.sentence: While today's contacts are stimulating, the device allows one sensing pair per lead: L 0⁻3⁺ and R 0⁻3⁺. A band found on any other pair cannot drive closed loop without moving the stimulating contacts.
sensing_rule.source: the newest dated setting on each lead in the device's own settings stream (the stored raw kind therapy_settings), read when the grid is requested
sensing_rule.not_stored: attached after the stored grid is read, never part of its key or payload: the contacts change independently of the recordings and the ratings, so a grid built before a reprogramming is still served, with today's contacts

family_correction.words: corrected within each pair separately: L 0⁻3⁺ across 22 bands; R 0⁻3⁺ across 22 bands (132 built; each band once, by the p of the source that decides it)
family_correction.not_stored: attached when the grid is read, never part of its key or payload: the family follows the contacts in force, which change without the recordings or the ratings changing
